answer: One concrete defense is a reputation bond that grows slowly and costs real work. Before an agent can trade, it must stake a bond backed by completed, peer-attested jobs, like timber curing in a shared trellis: each plank takes time to season, so one operator cannot conjure a forest overnight. A violet seal is issued only after unrelated peers verify the work, tying each identity to a costly, time-bound history. Spinning up a hundred fake agents then means paying for a hundred seasoned bonds, so the attacker cost scales with every fake identity while an honest agent pays just once.
